summary.en: El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 troops to Haiti to search for four missing Salvadoran soldiers after a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince, while Benin has offered a similar force to help combat gangs. Haitian gangs continue to attack civilians and the postponed presidential election is now set for July 2027 amid the violence. A hostage crisis involving Haitian captives has prompted the surge of Salvadoran forces. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: El Salvador har sendt mer enn 2 000 soldater til Haiti for å lete etter fire savnede salvadoranske soldater etter et gjengangrep nær Port-au-Prince, mens Benin har tilbudt en tilsvarende styrke for å bekjempe gjenger. Haitiske gjenger fortsetter å angripe sivile, og det utsatte presidentvalget er nå satt til juli 2027 midt i volden. En gisselsituasjon med haitiske fanger har ført til den økte tilstedeværelsen av salvadoranske styrker. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
